rows.requirement: Fulfillment is an extension (dev.ucp.shopping.fulfillment) that adds a fulfillment field to Checkout and/or Catalog (Catalog search/lookup added in 2026-08-25)
rows.quote: This extension adds a `fulfillment` field to Checkout and/or Catalog:
rows.notes: Lineage 2026-04-08->2026-08-25: doc moved fulfillment.md -> shopping/extensions/fulfillment.md. REWORDED (scope expanded): old text was 'This extension adds a `fulfillment` field to Checkout containing:' (Checkout only). New text is 'This extension adds a `fulfillment` field to Checkout and/or Catalog:' and the doc now explicitly documents a second, distinct field role on `dev.ucp.shopping.catalog.search`/`dev.ucp.shopping.catalog.lookup` (see new 'Catalog Discovery' section, L506-680) alongside the original Checkout role. Flagged for review: the extension's reach materially widened.

rows.requirement: fulfillment.methods[] holds fulfillment methods for cart items
rows.notes: Lineage: types/fulfillment.json stayed at the same relative path (source/schemas/shopping/types/fulfillment.json); methods field description text unchanged, line anchor shifted by ~1 line. NOTE: the file-level 'ucp_shared_request: true' annotation present in 2026-04-08 was dropped in 2026-08-25 (superseded by per-field ucp_request strings); does not affect this row's tested content.

rows.requirement: A fulfillment_method MUST include id, type, and line_item_ids
rows.quote:
"required": [
    "id",
    "type",
    "line_item_ids"
  ],
rows.notes: Lineage: fulfillment_method.json required array unchanged (id, type, line_item_ids), reformatted from single-line to multi-line array; same relative path.

rows.requirement: fulfillment_method.destinations[] lists addresses (shipping) or retail locations (pickup); selected_destination_id references the chosen one
rows.notes: Lineage: REWORDED. Old description (fulfillment_method.json 2026-04-08): 'Available destinations. For shipping: addresses. For pickup: retail locations.' New description: 'Available destinations for this method. In Business responses, each destination carries a `type` and `id`.' The old two-case (shipping=addresses / pickup=retail locations) phrasing was replaced by a generic self-describing-response statement, because 2026-08-25 adds an entire new '## Destinations' section (fulfillment.md L220-384) generalizing destination typing to any method (well-known `shipping_address`/`business_location` plus negotiated-extension values), superseding the old shipping/pickup-only framing. Also: the old 'Retail Location' concept/schema was renamed 'Business Location Destination' / location_destination.json (see FUL-005 vs old '#### Retail Location' heading, now '#### Business Location Destination'). official_oracle carried forward as true per prior fulfillment_test.py coverage of destination injection/selection; not re-verified against 2026-08-25 conformance suite in this pass. Flagged for review.

rows.requirement: fulfillment_method.groups[] are merchant-generated packages; agent sets selected_option_id on groups to choose shipping method
rows.notes: Lineage: fulfillment_method.json groups field description unchanged verbatim; same relative path, line anchor shifted.

rows.requirement: A fulfillment_group MUST include id and line_item_ids
rows.quote: "required": ["id", "line_item_ids"],
rows.notes: Lineage: fulfillment_group.json required array unchanged verbatim; same relative path and line.

rows.requirement: A fulfillment_option MUST include id, title, and totals
rows.quote: "required": ["id", "title"],
rows.notes: Lineage: RENAMED/restructured. In 2026-04-08, fulfillment_option.json alone required ["id","title","totals"]. In 2026-08-25, fulfillment_option.json was decomposed: a NEW shared file fulfillment_option_base.json (title 'Fulfillment Option Base') now requires ["id","title"] (quoted here, L7), and fulfillment_option.json composes it via 'allOf' with a second branch requiring ["totals"] (fulfillment_option.json L13: "required": ["totals"]). The effective combined requirement (id, title, totals all required on a checkout fulfillment_option) is IDENTICAL to 2026-04-08 — only the schema's file/composition structure changed (fulfillment_option_base.json is also reused directly by the new Catalog Discovery 'options[]' shape, per fulfillment.md L580-582). Cites the base file as the more novel change; see FUL-017 for the sibling 'totals' requirement's own prose-level rename.

rows.requirement: options[].title is the required primary label that distinguishes the option from its siblings
rows.quote: | `groups[].options[]`  | `title`       | Yes      | Primary label that distinguishes from siblings          |
rows.notes: Lineage: Rendering table row unchanged verbatim; doc moved fulfillment.md -> shopping/extensions/fulfillment.md.

rows.requirement: options[].title MUST distinguish this option from its siblings
rows.quote: * **MUST** distinguish this option from its siblings

rows.requirement: options[].title SHOULD include method and speed
rows.quote: * **SHOULD** include method and speed (e.g., "Express Shipping", "Curbside Pickup")

rows.requirement: options[].title MUST be sufficient for buyer decision if description is absent
rows.quote: * **MUST** be sufficient for buyer decision if `description` is absent

rows.requirement: options[].description MUST NOT repeat title or total; provides supplementary context only
rows.quote: * **MUST NOT** repeat `title` or `total`—provides supplementary context only
rows.notes: Lineage: unchanged verbatim (note: this bullet still says singular `total` in prose even though the Rendering table's field name changed to `totals` -- see FUL-017; this specific bullet's wording did not change so it is carried as-is).

rows.requirement: options[].description SHOULD include timing, carrier, or other decision-relevant details
rows.quote: * **SHOULD** include timing, carrier, or other decision-relevant details

rows.requirement: options[].description SHOULD be a complete phrase
rows.quote: * **SHOULD** be a complete phrase (e.g., "Arrives Dec 12-15 via FedEx")

rows.requirement: options[].description MAY be omitted if title is self-explanatory
rows.quote: * **MAY** be omitted if title is self-explanatory

rows.requirement: options[].totals is the required cost breakdown (an array of `total` objects), replacing the old prose name `total` (a nullable scalar)
rows.quote: | `groups[].options[]`  | `totals`      | Yes      | Cost breakdown: an array of `total` objects             |
rows.notes: Lineage: RENAMED (resolves the divergence the 2026-04-08 row itself flagged). Old Rendering-table row: '| `groups[].options[]`  | `total`       | Yes      | Price in minor units (may be null if not yet available) |' -- the prose named a singular, nullable scalar field `total` even though the schema's actual field was always the array `totals`. New row: '| `groups[].options[]`  | `totals`      | Yes      | Cost breakdown: an array of `total` objects             |' -- prose now uses the correct plural field name `totals` (an array of `total` objects) matching fulfillment_option.json's actual required 'totals' field, and drops the 'may be null if not yet available' nullability language entirely. This is a genuine identifier rename (total -> totals) plus a description rewrite; it converges prose and schema that previously diverged.

rows.requirement: available_methods[].description MUST be a standalone sentence explaining what, when, and where
rows.quote: * **MUST** be a standalone sentence explaining what, when, and where

rows.requirement: available_methods[].description SHOULD be usable verbatim in platform dialogue
rows.quote:
* **SHOULD** be usable verbatim in platform dialogue (e.g., "Pants available
    for pickup at Downtown Store today at 2pm")

rows.requirement: Businesses SHOULD return options[] in a meaningful (business) order
rows.quote:
* Businesses **SHOULD** return `options[]` in a meaningful order (e.g., cheapest
    first, fastest first)

rows.requirement: Platforms SHOULD preserve the business-provided option order by default, but MAY re-order options (e.g. to match buyer preferences or surface ranking); platforms MUST preserve the method/option grouping regardless of reordering
rows.notes: Lineage: REWORDED (material change, weakens the old rule). Old text: 'Platforms **SHOULD** render options in the provided order.' New text explicitly permits reordering: 'Platforms **SHOULD** preserve that order, but **MAY** re-order it (e.g. to match known buyer preferences or surface-specific ranking); they **MUST** preserve the method/option grouping.' The old row was a plain SHOULD-preserve-order rule; the new text keeps a SHOULD-preserve-default but adds an explicit MAY-reorder carve-out plus a new MUST about preserving grouping. Flagged for review.

rows.requirement: Platforms SHOULD treat fulfillment as a generic, renderable structure: render each option using title/description/total; present all methods returned; preserve the method/option structure without merging or de-duplicating (the platform, not the business's provided order, now chooses ordering); use available_methods[].description to surface alternatives
rows.quote:
Platforms **SHOULD** treat fulfillment as a generic, renderable structure: ... Preserve the method and option structure—do not merge or de-duplicate;
    the platform chooses ordering
rows.notes: Lineage: REWORDED (one sub-bullet reversed). Old Platform Responsibilities bullets (fulfillment.md 2026-04-08 L203-207) included 'Present options in the order provided by the business' as a sub-requirement of the generic-renderable-structure SHOULD. In 2026-08-25 that bullet is REMOVED and replaced with 'Preserve the method and option structure—do not merge or de-duplicate; the platform chooses ordering' -- i.e. ordering authority flips from the business (provided order) to the platform (chooses ordering), consistent with the new FUL-021 MAY-reorder carve-out. The intro sentence and the 'present all methods returned' / 'use available_methods[].description' bullets are unchanged. Flagged for review.

rows.requirement: Platforms MAY provide enhanced UX for recognized method types; baseline contract is title + description + total is sufficient to render any option
rows.quote:
Platforms **MAY** provide enhanced UX for recognized method types (store
selectors
for pickup, carrier logos for shipping), but this is optional. The baseline
contract is: **`title` + `description` + `total` is sufficient to render any
option.**

rows.requirement: When a buyer selects an option the platform cannot fully process, the platform SHOULD use continue_url to hand off to the business's checkout
rows.quote:
When a buyer selects an option the platform cannot fully process, the
platform **SHOULD** use `continue_url` to hand off to the business's checkout.

rows.requirement: If the buyer chooses pickup but the platform does not support split fulfillment, the platform SHOULD use continue_url to hand off to the business's checkout
rows.quote:
If the buyer chooses pickup but the platform doesn't support split
fulfillment, the platform **SHOULD** use `continue_url` to hand off to the
business's checkout.

rows.requirement: When supports_multi_group is false (default), the business MUST consolidate all items into a single group per method
rows.quote: * Business **MUST** consolidate all items into a **single group per method**

rows.requirement: When supports_multi_group is false, the business MAY still return multiple methods (e.g., shipping + pickup) if cart items require it
rows.quote:
* Business **MAY** still return multiple methods (e.g., shipping + pickup) if
    cart items require it

rows.requirement: When supports_multi_group is true, the business MAY return multiple groups per method based on inventory, packaging, or warehouse logic
rows.quote:
* Business **MAY** return multiple groups per method based on inventory,
    packaging, or warehouse logic

rows.requirement: A shipping_destination MUST include id and type (type is a required const discriminator "shipping_address"); it is a postal_address plus required id and type
rows.quote:
"required": [
        "id",
        "type"
      ]
rows.notes: Lineage: REWORDED/expanded. Old shipping_destination.json (2026-04-08) required only ["id"] and had no `type` field at all. New shipping_destination.json (2026-08-25) requires ["id", "type"] and adds a `type` property (`"const": "shipping_address"`, description 'Destination type discriminator.'). This is the schema-level counterpart of the new '## Destinations' section's self-describing-response rule (fulfillment.md: 'in Business responses, every destination carries a required `type`'). The old row's parenthetical ('it is a postal_address plus a required id') is no longer complete: it is now a postal_address plus required id AND type. Flagged for review as a substantive addition, not just a rename.
